coachMessages.text: Two threats, same column. One is higher, one is lower. Gravity fills bottom-up — which threat gets there first?

slides.infoProse:
<board instructions>Show a simple position where Gray has a horizontal major threat completing at col 3 row 0 (even-indexed) and Green has a horizontal major threat completing at col 3 row 1 (odd-indexed). Col 3 is empty. Mark Gray's threat cell at row 0 with 'tg' (your threat, fires first) and Green's threat cell at row 1 with 'td' (dead — can never be reached). Legend: 'tg' = Gray's lower threat (fires first — the undercut), 'td' = Green's upper threat (killed by gravity).</board instructions>

Gravity fills columns bottom-up. Whoever owns the lower cell in a column gets there first — period. Gray's threat at row 0 fires the instant any disc enters column 3. Green's threat at row 1 will never be reached, because Gray wins the moment the column is touched. The lower threat kills the upper threat.

coachMessages.text: You don't find an undercut — you build one. Arrange your three-in-a-row so it completes at the cell directly below their threat.

slides.infoProse:
<board instructions>Show a mid-game position (10–14 moves played) where Green already has three discs forming a horizontal line whose completing cell is col C row 3 (odd-indexed). Gray's three discs form a horizontal line whose completing cell is also col C but at row 2 (even-indexed — directly below Green's threat). Gray has not yet played the winning move. Mark Green's threat cell at row 3 with 'td' (will be killed) and Gray's threat cell at row 2 with 'tg' (wins first). Legend: 'tg' = Gray's undercut threat (row 2 — fires first), 'td' = Green's threat (row 3 — killed by Gray's lower threat).</board instructions>

You don't find an undercut — you build one. By arranging your three-in-a-row to complete at the cell directly below your opponent's threat, you own that column. Whoever plays into col C, Gray wins at row 2 before Green ever reaches row 3. The undercut is a weapon you construct during the setup phase.

coachMessages.text: When both threats land on rows of the same parity (both even or both odd), neither kills the other — both must be blocked separately.

slides.infoProse:
<board instructions>Show a position where Gray has a horizontal major threat completing at col 3 row 0 (even-indexed) and Green also has a horizontal major threat completing at col 3 row 2 (also even-indexed). Both threat cells are in the same column but two rows apart, both on even rows. Mark both cells with 'tg' overlays (both live — both must be blocked). Legend: 'tg' = Both threats are live (same parity — neither kills the other).</board instructions>

The undercut only works when your threat is on the *opposite* parity row to theirs — one even, one odd. When both threats land on the same parity (both even rows like 0 and 2, or both odd rows like 1 and 3), neither kills the other. Both remain alive and your opponent must block them separately. Check the row numbers: if they share parity, no undercut is possible.

coachMessages.text: One Gray disc sits below Green's threat — but is that an undercut? What makes a real undercut?

slides.infoProse:
<board instructions>Show a position where Green has a horizontal major threat completing at col C row 1. Gray has a single disc in col C row 0 (directly below Green's threat), but that Gray disc is NOT part of any three-in-a-row — there is no Gray major threat at row 0. Mark the Gray disc at row 0 with 'td' ('Lone disc — no undercut') and Green's threat cell at row 1 with 'tg' ('Green's threat — still live'). Legend: 'td' = Gray's lone disc (does NOT constitute an undercut), 'tg' = Green's threat (still dangerous).</board instructions>

Occupying the cell below your opponent's threat does not create an undercut. You need a real winning threat at that cell — three Gray discs that would form four-in-a-row there. A single disc below their threat does nothing: Green can still complete their threat freely because Gray has no counter-threat to fear. Build the full three-in-a-row first, then the cell becomes an undercut.

socratic.goalPrompt: Which column lets Gray win by undercutting Green's threat — placing Gray's winning cell directly below Green's?
socratic._boardInstructions: Show a mid-game position (10–14 discs total) where col 2 has exactly 2 discs already placed (rows 0–1 filled, row 2 is the next playable cell). Red has a horizontal major threat completing at col 2 row 3 (odd-indexed), and Yellow has a horizontal major threat completing at col 2 row 2 (even-indexed, directly below — the very next cell in the column). Mark Yellow's row-2 cell with 'tg' (fires immediately — the undercut) and Red's row-3 cell with 'td' (killed by gravity; col 2 row 3 is never reached because Yellow wins the instant the column is touched). Legend: 'tg' = Yellow's winning cell (lower threat, fires first), 'td' = Red's dead threat (upper, blocked). Yellow plays col 2 to win instantly.
